ascorbic acid.t: Thiamine, riboflavin, pyridoxine, niacinamide, and ascorbic acid decrease activities of erythromycin, kanamycin, streptomycin, doxycycline, and lincomycin ( 7.1 )
Ascorbic acid and riboflavin may reduce the activity of bleomycin ( 7.1 )

doxycycline.t: Thiamine, riboflavin, pyridoxine, niacinamide, and ascorbic acid decrease activities of erythromycin, kanamycin, streptomycin, doxycycline, and lincomycin ( 7.1 )
Thiamine, riboflavin, pyridoxine, niacinamide, and ascorbic acid decrease antibiotic activities of erythromycin, kanamycin, streptomycin, doxycycline, and lincomycin.

erythromycin.t: Thiamine, riboflavin, pyridoxine, niacinamide, and ascorbic acid decrease activities of erythromycin, kanamycin, streptomycin, doxycycline, and lincomycin ( 7.1 )
Thiamine, riboflavin, pyridoxine, niacinamide, and ascorbic acid decrease antibiotic activities of erythromycin, kanamycin, streptomycin, doxycycline, and lincomycin.

streptomycin.t: Thiamine, riboflavin, pyridoxine, niacinamide, and ascorbic acid decrease activities of erythromycin, kanamycin, streptomycin, doxycycline, and lincomycin ( 7.1 )
Thiamine, riboflavin, pyridoxine, niacinamide, and ascorbic acid decrease antibiotic activities of erythromycin, kanamycin, streptomycin, doxycycline, and lincomycin.

levodopa.t: Pyridoxine may decrease blood levels of levodopa and levodopa efficacy may decrease ( 7.1 )
Pyridoxine may increase the metabolism of levodopa (decrease blood levels of levodopa) and decrease its efficacy.

folic acid.t: Avoid the use of multiple vitamins injection (adult) in patients with suspected or diagnosed megaloblastic anemia prior to blood sampling for the detection of the folic acid and cyanocobalamin deficiencies.
Folic acid may decrease phenytoin blood levels and increase risk of seizure activity ( 7.1 )

phenytoin.t: Folic acid may decrease phenytoin blood levels and increase risk of seizure activity ( 7.1 )
Folic acid may increase phenytoin metabolism and lower the serum concentration of phenytoin resulting in increased seizure activity.

methotrexate.t: Folic acid may decrease response to methotrexate ( 7.1 ) Effects of other drugs on multiple vitamins injection (adult):
Folic acid may decrease a patient’s response to methotrexate therapy.

hydralazine.t: Concomitant administration of hydralazine or isoniazid may increase pyridoxine requirements ( 7.2 ).
Concomitant administration of hydralazine or isoniazid may increase pyridoxine requirements.

isoniazid.t: Concomitant administration of hydralazine or isoniazid may increase pyridoxine requirements ( 7.2 ).
Concomitant administration of hydralazine or isoniazid may increase pyridoxine requirements.

warfarin.t: In patients who are co-administered warfarin and multiple vitamins injection (adult), blood levels of prothrombin/INR should be monitored to determine if dose of warfarin needs to be adjusted [see Warnings and Precautions ( 5.4 )].

chloramphenicol.t: In patients with pernicious anemia, the hematologic response to vitamin B 12 therapy may be inhibited by chloramphenicol.

glucose.t: Ascorbic acid in the urine may cause false negative urine glucose results.

vitamin a.t: Hypervitaminosis A Hypervitaminosis A, manifested by nausea, vomiting, headache, dizziness, blurred vision has been reported in patients with renal failure receiving 1.5 mg/day retinol and in patients with liver disease, Therefore, supplementation of renal failure patients and patients with liver disease with vitamin A, an ingredient found in multiple vitamins injection (adult), should be undertaken with caution [ see Use in Specific Populations ( 8.6 and 8.7 ) ].

anticoag.t: 5.4 Decreased Anticoagulant Effect of Warfarin Multiple vitamins injection (adult) contains Vitamin K, which may decrease the anticoagulant action of warfarin.

thiazide.t: Multiple vitamins injection (adult) is not physically compatible with moderately alkaline solutions such as a sodium bicarbonate solution and other alkaline drugs such as acetazolamide sodium, aminophylline, ampicillin sodium, tetracycline HCl and chlorothiazide sodium.
